summary.headline: Vijaya Diagnostic Q2 FY27 revenue rose 26.7% YoY to about INR 255 crore, with EBITDA margin at 44.1%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was about INR 255 crore, up 26.7% YoY, driven by 16.5% volume growth, favourable test mix and CGHS tariff revision. EBITDA rose 37.8% YoY to about INR 113 crore at a 44.1% margin (up 350 bps), and PAT was INR 59 crore (23.3% margin). H1 revenue was INR 486 crore (+24.8%) and H1 EBITDA INR 211 crore (+36%). Management signed a BTA to acquire Arya Wellness Centre in Guwahati, its entry into the Northeast, and laid out a capex plan of 8 hubs and 14 spokes by Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Hyderabad
segments.commentary: Contributed 67% of Q2 revenue (69% a year earlier) and grew over 20% YoY; mid-teens volume growth plus 2-3% mix benefit. Around 100 centres, including 19 hubs.

segments.name: Rest of AP and Telangana
segments.commentary: Contributed about 20% of revenue; 33 centres, of which 15 hubs and 18 spokes.

segments.name: Pune
segments.commentary: Contributed 5% of revenue and grew about 15.5% YoY; management cites double-digit growth over the last 3-4 quarters and PH (acquired) margin above 35%.

segments.name: West Bengal (Kolkata)
segments.commentary: Contributed 5% of revenue; 12 centres (7 hubs, 5 spokes).

segments.name: Radiology and Pathology
segments.commentary: Radiology about 37% of revenue, pathology the balance (about 63%); B2C is 92% of revenue. Wellness is about 14.5% of revenue and grew over 25% in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of at least 20% described as fairly achievable, against H1 growth of about 25%.
Long-term (3-5 years) revenue growth guidance of above 15%, with about 13% from price and volume contributing the rest; existing networks 8-10% and new centres 3-3.5%.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected at 42% and above, after H1 at 43-44%.
Price hike not yet taken; decision on Q3 or Q4 to be made after comparing prices with the market.
Capex of INR 155-160 crore for 8 hubs and 14 spokes by Q1 FY28: 2 hubs done, 3 more by March 2027, 3 in Q1 FY28.
FY28 plan of 4-5 hubs plus a few spokes, including a third Hyderabad flagship (lease signed, opening in 6-8 months).

Arya Wellness (Guwahati) acquisition expected to close in about two months; the acquired hub has revenue above INR 25 crore and EBITDA above 20% (pre-Ind AS). Management will share the transaction and strategy details next quarter.
capex_capacity: Expansion capex of INR 155-160 crore for 8 hubs and 14 spokes by Q1 FY28; 2 hubs commissioned so far in H1, including the JP Nagar flagship in Bengaluru.
Panjagutta central lab with automated track system (about INR 20 crore) to be operational in the next few months.

Pune: new Market Yard hub with central lab (INR 18-20 crore) targeted for FY27; relocation of Satara and Mayur Colony hubs to larger premises; INR 19 crore purchase of a building near Mayur Colony, commissioning in FY28.
Kadapa (Tier-2, AP) land bought for about INR 9 crore; hub planned within two years.
Two CT units upgraded to 160-slice cardiac CT. Second MRI planned for Tirupati within six months; Omega 3T MRI being considered for the third Hyderabad flagship.
Asset-light model retained, but one or two prime hub locations in Pune, Bengaluru or Kolkata may be owned.
demand_pricing: Q2 growth split: about 16-16.5% volume, 4-5% favourable test mix (high-end CT and CT angio), about 3% from the CGHS tariff hike from late 2025.
Pricing history: historical price realisation CAGR about 2%; last price hike was June 2025.
Management says competitors are not adding centres at Vijaya's pace in Hyderabad; high-end pathology such as genomics faces little competition from smaller centres.
Wellness is growing above 20% historically and is now mostly packages sold at a slight discount, so it is not a major driver of revenue per test.
Revenue per test rose to INR 513 in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Given FY27 guidance of high-teens to 20% and H1 run-rate of about 25%, how should the full year and H2 be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 growth of at least 20% is fairly achievable. Long-term guidance is above 15%, mostly from volume, with price adding about 2% a year.

qa_highlights.question: How many hubs and spokes are planned for FY28, and where?
qa_highlights.answer: About 4-5 hubs in FY28 on top of this year's 8, plus a few spokes, including a third Hyderabad flagship. Expansion is concentrated in the core geographies and the new metros, not new states.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 44% EBITDA margin and how far can it go?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating leverage, since about 65-70% of costs are fixed. The CGHS tariff hike added about 2%. Management expects FY27 margin of 42% and above.

qa_highlights.question: Why does Hyderabad keep growing, and what is the role of mix versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is from brand, market share gains from unorganised players, new modalities (open MRI, dual-source CT) and additional equipment such as second ultrasound and MRI units. Management said price is not the driver.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Arya Wellness margin and plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The Guwahati hub is doing above 20% pre-Ind AS EBITDA with revenue above INR 25 crore. Management will give transaction and strategy details once the deal closes, expected in about two months.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company plan to add 10 hubs a year, and will new clusters match Hyderabad's margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management asked investors not to model 10 hubs a year; the norm is 4-5 hubs a year. New hubs are reaching break-even within the set timelines, so there is no margin concern.

risks_watch: Revenue growth depends on volume; price hike timing is undecided and price adds only about 2% a year historically.
Hyderabad still provides 67% of revenue, though the share is falling by about 2 points a year.
Capex of INR 155-160 crore plus other projects (Panjagutta lab, Pune hubs, property purchase, Kadapa land) and more owned premises may pressure cash and the asset-light model.
Hub ramp-up pace across 8 hubs in H2 FY27 and Q1 FY28, and whether new hubs keep reaching break-even on schedule.
Arya Wellness deal completion in about two months and disclosure of its economics next quarter.
Wellness share is flat around 14.5% of revenue, with management noting a reporting-definition risk.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volume growth, margins and the expansion pipeline. Management was more measured on long-term price assumptions and on the Arya deal, deferring details until closing.
key_quotes: So, we are fairly confident that for this financial year, we will be growing at least like a 20% growth rate is fairly achievable for this financial year.

The beauty of our model is, most of our expenses are fixed in nature, close to like a 65%-70% of our expenses are fixed in nature, which is allowing this operating leverage to play out whenever revenue is growing beyond that 15% to 18%.
So, our option is always to take it on lease. There is no change in the strategy.

Panjagutta central lab with automated track system (~INR 20 cr) operational in next few months

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of at least 20% as 'fairly achievable' (below H1's ~25%), backed by 2 of 8 hubs already live, 8 hubs and 14 spokes (INR 155-160 cr) by Q1 FY28, 16-16.5% volume growth and ~3% CGHS tariff uplift; guidance is 'cut' vs prior, and EBITDA margin guided at 42%+ for FY27 vs H1 43-44%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 EBITDA margin was 43.4% and Q2 44.1%, but management guides FY27 at 42%+, implying H2 margin flat to lower as new hubs ramp and price hike is undecided; operating leverage on ~65-70% fixed costs is the upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 8 hubs and 14 spokes (INR 155-160 cr) under way with 2 hubs done, 3 more by March 2027 and 3 in Q1 FY28; Panjagutta lab (~INR 20 cr) due in the next few months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 volume grew 16.5% YoY and Hyderabad grew over 20% with mid-teens volume growth, backed by 8 hubs and 14 spokes coming live and share gains from unorganised players.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex already committed at INR 155-160 cr, with a further 4-5 hubs planned for FY28 plus a second Tirupati MRI within six months and Pune Market Yard lab (INR 18-20 cr) targeted for FY27.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 growth guidance was framed as 'at least 20%' and 'fairly achievable', below H1's ~25%, and FY27 margin guide of 42%+ sits below H1's 43-44%; management did not signal a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Price hike is undecided (last taken June 2025), price adds only ~2% a year, and CGHS tariff uplift (~3%) is a one-off tailwind; a slowdown in volume or hub ramp-up could pressure the 20% growth floor.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is adding new modalities (open MRI, dual-source CT, 160-slice cardiac CT upgrades) and a second Tirupati MRI within six months, with an Omega 3T MRI under consideration for the third Hyderabad flagship.

rows.label: Arya Wellness (Guwahati) entry into Northeast
rows.why: BTA signed; acquired hub has revenue above INR 25 cr and pre-Ind AS EBITDA above 20%, with deal completion expected in about two months.

rows.label: Price hike decision for Q3 or Q4
rows.why: Price hike not yet taken (last June 2025) and historical price realisation CAGR is only ~2%; decision depends on market price comparison.

rows.label: Operating leverage on fixed-cost base
rows.why: About 65-70% of costs are fixed, and Q2 EBITDA rose 37.8% YoY on 26.7% revenue growth, so margin gains continue as volume rises.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume growth, margins and the hub pipeline, and cautious on long-term price and the Arya deal economics, deferring details until closing; analysts pushed on how to model FY27 and H2 given the 25% H1 run-rate, and on the 10-hubs-a-year pace.
